text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: High-severity alert — multiple ELB target groups in eu-west-1b reporting healthy=0/targets. Source: ELB healthcheck failures + instance metadata timeouts. Incident INC-2026-0421. Paging oncall: @ryan (primary), @santiago (backup).
ryan: saw the page, joining. brief summary pls — is traffic dropping or is it healthchecks only?
santiago: quick check — ELB logs show 504s from targets and healthcheck probes failing with TCP timeout. control-plane console shows a bunch of EC2 metadata (IMDS) timeouts in the azb region.
luke: adding context: we've seen a handful of autoscaling groups in eu-west-1b where lifecycle hooks are stuck because instances can't reach IMDS; that prevents new targets from registering properly.
kai: can we confirm if EBS or underlying network is impacted? cloudwatch shows EBS metrics normal, but ENI-level packet drops on a subset of hosts.
ryan: ok, two root causes possible: (1) IMDS throttling or network path to 169.254.169.254 in azb is saturated -> apps fail to refresh creds/healthchecks, (2) noisy neighbor on ENI egress. we need quick mitigation: route traffic away from azb.
santiago: recommend immediate Route53 weight shift away from eu-west-1b pools to a/b/c across eu-west-1a and 1c, set weights to 0 for azb. who can run the change?
maria: I can update DNS weights on status page and infra console. Will also add an explanatory note.
luke: before you shift, note that some customers pinned endpoints to ELB DNS that map to AZ-local IPs. But weighted routing should steer client connections to healthy AZs if they use the regional CNAME. still worth doing.
ryan: do it. maria, set Route53 weights to 0 for azb and increase others to compensate. also flip any AWS ALB cross-zone load-balancing toggles if needed.
maria: making change now — running terraform apply to route53-weights. snippet: ```
resource "aws_route53_record" "svc-weight-eu-west1" {
  name = "svc.example.com"
  type = "CNAME"
  set_identifier = "eu-west-1b"
  weight = 0
}
```
statuspage-bot: Draft update: "Investigating elevated errors for customers in EU (eu-west-1). Traffic being shifted away from affected availability zone while we investigate. No customer data impact identified at this time." Shall I publish?
cs-lead: publish now and tag enterprise customers with a heads-up. have support queue monitor affected customers.
ryan: while DNS is changing, let's mitigate at the infra level: santiago, can you push an isolate on the problematic ENI pool to prevent further noisy neighbor effects? If we cordon nodes that show >5% packet drop.
santiago: running query to list ENIs in azb with >5% drop: ```aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=tag:az,Values=eu-west-1b Name=tag:role,Values=serving | jq '.NetworkInterfaces[] | select(.Status=="in-use")'``` will evict by ASG subsequently.
luke: also recommend enabling ALB failover to secondary target groups for a couple of services that have multi-AZ replicas. adding canary traffic to verify.
kai: I've seen IMDS logs showing 429 responses from IMDS on those hosts — likely metadata endpoint rate limit or local path congested. reaching out to AWS support (case 1234567890) concurrently.
maria: Route53 change applied, weights now set to 0 for eu-west-1b. propagation looks good — ~60% of traffic away from azb within 30s, 95% by 2m.
ryan: good. CS — notify customers who saw errors in last 15m. ops: continue evicting ENIs and draining instances where IMDS fails persist. note: don't drain database hosts unless confirmed.
santiago: evict plan started: set ASG desired capacity to maintain production in the other AZs, then terminate problematic instances in batches of 5, letting ASG spawn replacements in other AZs.
statuspage-bot: Live update published.
cs-lead: ticket template for customers: "We're aware of elevated 50x/504 errors in EU region; we've shifted traffic and are investigating; ETA next update 20 minutes."
kai: AWS support says they're investigating a regional network fabric issue affecting IMDS and intra-AZ routing in eu-west-1b. They suggested a mitigation: isolate affected hosts and rely on cross-AZ routing.
ryan: timeline for full recovery? until ENI packet loss drops and IMDS stabilizes, we keep weights 0. start planning rollback once IMDS 200s are stable for 10 minutes across samples.
maria: I'll keep status page and slack thread updated. next update in 10 mins or earlier if status changes.
ryan: switching to incident channel for postmortem. oncall handoff: @santiago will take lead in 30m; I'm handing off now to run higher-level coordination with AWS. Thanks everyone — great triage. :thumbsup:
